title: Genesys AI and bots
summary: Dialog Engine and digital bots, failure paths, Agent Copilot, tokens, and the AI exams as the catalog names them.

lessons.title: Two Architect bot types, plus Copilot beside the agent
lessons.summary: A bot flow talks to the customer. Agent Copilot talks to the agent. They are different products on different pages.
paras: Architect documents Genesys Dialog Engine Bot Flows and Genesys Digital Bot Flows as flow types. An inbound flow calls them with the matching action. Agent Copilot, on its own overview, works inside the agent experience: knowledge, transcripts, scripts, next best action, and notes. Copilot is part of the CX 4 story on the package overview, along with Journey Management and a published token allotment.

Do not design a “bot” and assume it covers both. A voice bot that cannot reach a queue is a trapped caller. A Copilot summary that Virtual Supervisor reuses is a billing note on the STA FAQ, not a second bot.

lessons.title: Dialog Engine bot flows are voice and digital intents
lessons.summary: You build the bot in Architect, then the inbound flow calls it.
paras: The Dialog Engine article and the inbound-bot article show a bot that asks a question and returns an intent the flow can branch on. The banking example checks a balance or finds a branch. Voice speaks the question. Chat displays it. Intents are outcomes, not a hidden script the ACD can guess.

Call Bot Flow is the action for this bot type. A digital-only bot uses a different action, covered next. Give every no-match, timeout, and error output a queue. Flow Insights, after you publish, shows whether anyone reached the bot.

lessons.title: Digital bot flows are a different call
lessons.summary: Message experiences use Digital Bot Flows and Call Digital Bot Flow.
paras: The digital bot article describes Genesys Digital Bot Flows for message experiences. They are Architect flows, and they are not the Dialog Engine type with a renamed action. An inbound message flow calls them with Call Digital Bot Flow. Mixing the actions is a publish-time or runtime miss, not a wording preference.

Digital bots still need a human path. The message queue, the in-queue message flow, and the error-event queue from the Architect create-flow rules still apply. A bot that handles the first turn does not delete those requirements.

lessons.title: Every bot has a failure output to a queue
lessons.summary: No-match, timeout, and error are normal. The queue is the design.
paras: The inbound bot article’s useful pattern is a question, an intent, and a way out. Treat failure as a path you draw, not as an exception. After hours, the way out may be a different queue or a callback, still inside Architect, still published.

External bot connectors exist as a separate action family. The list changes. This lab will not name a vendor. Confirm the connector in Architect, and still draw the failure output. A connector timeout is the same caller problem as a no-match.

lessons.title: Agent Copilot assists the person who stayed on the interaction
lessons.summary: Knowledge, transcripts, scripts, next best action, and notes. The benefit is described as surviving a blind transfer.
paras: The Agent Copilot overview lists knowledge articles, transcripts, custom scripts, next best action, and forms and notes: reason, resolution, and a possible wrap-up. It is help for the agent, grounded in content you maintain. A knowledge article that is wrong will be repeated confidently. Curate the source.

The overview says the benefits survive a blind transfer, so the next agent is not starting from an empty panel. That is not a reason to blind-transfer a payment. Secure flows still exist to keep digits out of recordings and out of participant data. Copilot does not collect card numbers.

lessons.title: Tokens are a published allotment, and a FAQ ratio you re-read
lessons.summary: The overview publishes CX 4 token counts. The STA FAQ publishes how AI scoring spends them.
paras: The package overview lists 30 AI tokens for a named CX 4 user and 39 for a concurrent user. That sentence is the allotment story. The STA FAQ says AI scoring needs STA, quality management, and AI Experience Tokens, and that one token covers 20 AI-scored evaluations. It also says a Copilot summary reused by Virtual Supervisor is not billed twice. Re-read both pages before you put a number in a contract.

Bots are not the same meter. Do not assume a Dialog Engine flow spends the scoring token. If a page does not say it, this lab will not say it. Fair use is a third page, for pooled allowances such as API requests and transcription, and it is not the token table.

lessons.title: The AI exams are named on the catalog, one exam each
lessons.summary: Two AI certifications. No invented exam codes.
paras: The Genesys Cloud exams page lists AI certifications separately from the Professional and Developer certifications and from the specialist exams. As read on 14 October 2026, each of AI – GPE & GPR and Digital Bots & Knowledge is one exam. The catalog links them to course 17671 and course 18174. This lab does not invent a GCX- prefix for either.

Speech and Text Analytics is a specialist certification on the same catalog, not one of those two AI exams. Passing a bot course does not pass the STA specialist exam. The announcement page covers webcam and practice-exam notes. Read it before you book.
lessons.uncertainty: Course numbers were taken from the Genesys Cloud exams catalog as read on 14 October 2026. Confirm before you enroll.
